angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,055,377 km at 77.43 pc = 0.18 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 12.9142 +/- 0.0177 mas (same row, RUWE 0.90): 77.43 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.517 +/- 0.038 solar radii from Kane et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HD 17156 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..252K/abstract): 1,055,377 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.285 +/- 0.064 solar masses from Kane et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HD 17156 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..252K/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6046 +/- 76 K from Kane et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 17156 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..252K/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Kane et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 17156 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..252K/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hd-17156.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.185, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 17156 (pscomppars): spectral type G5, from Ment et al. 2018 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156..213M/abstract)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, HD 17156: main object type PM*, High Proper Motion Star
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 17156 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.208 dex, from Kane et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..252K/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 17156 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units 0.44091, from Kane et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..252K/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 17156 (pscomppars): age 3.3 Gyr, from Kane et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..252K/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 17156 (pscomppars): rotation period 12.8 d, from Fischer et al. 2007 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2007ApJ...669.1336F/abstract)

rotationPeriodsCatalogued.source: VizieR J/A+A/705/A142/tablea1 (Physical properties study of planet systems), column Prot: 12.8 d, the row 0.0 arcsec from the star's J2000 place

projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 17156 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 2.8 km/s, from Bonomo et al. 2017 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017A&A...602A.107B/abstract)
spinInclinationSource: Computed here from this record's rotation period, projected rotation speed and radius (1.517 solar radii): sin i = v sin i × P / (2πR) = 0.467. Not a measurement of the axis: the three numbers come from different papers.

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
